sources.origin: Tesla Q2 2026 production, deliveries and deployments

claims.claim: Tesla spans two distinct infrastructure chains: vehicle manufacturing converts battery/electronics/software capacity into mobility, while energy storage converts cell/power-electronics capacity into grid flexibility; shared manufacturing and battery inputs create leverage but also correlated resource constraints.

Q2 deliveries above production indicate inventory conversion in the vehicle chain, whereas storage deployment is a separate execution vector; structural resilience should therefore be tested across both chains rather than inferred from aggregate delivery headlines.

causalEdges.mechanism: electric vehicles provide transport using battery/electronic/software systems
storage shifts power across time and supports variable generation/load
shared industrial inputs constrain and enable both vehicle and storage scaling

risks: vehicle demand and storage demand have different economics
inventory drawdown can temporarily lift deliveries above production
battery/input constraints can correlate across divisions
competitive EV and storage substitutes remain credible
contradictions: Vehicle delivery outperformance and roughly in-line storage execution show uneven strength across Tesla's two major physical scaling vectors.
unknowns: margin contribution of Q2 vehicle mix
durability and economics of storage growth
falsifiers: delivery strength that repeatedly depends on inventory drawdown rather than sustainable production/demand
storage deployment growth without durable economic contribution or with worsening shared-input constraints

recommendation.reason: Beta causal mapping is complete; profitability and valuation treatment remain Alpha-owned.
